Horrible Food and Disgusting Customer Service

We visited Beirut Restaurant as a family and ordered two or three dishes, including the mutton fatayer. The mutton in the fatayer appeared undercooked, almost raw, and one bite made me feel sick.

We raised the issue with the staff, but they were rude and unhelpful. They refused to refund us, charged us for the dish, and packed it for takeaway despite our complaint. When I said I would share our experience in a review, a staff member replied, “Do whatever you want.”

We left disappointed by both the food and the way our concern was handled. Based on this visit, I would not recommend the restaurant. I’ve attached photos of the food, bill, and restaurant for reference.

I've ordered hummus, Foul and Fattah; the teast is almost the worst, lacks od any teast, plain like eating raw food! You need to pay for everything even onions, olives, pickles and tomatos. And they don't serve lemon which a big shame since its 101 to served with these dishes! Some of the pickles have now salt, which is first time for me! Tea teast is bellow average and came almost cold woth tiny cubs. Bread isn't freshly backed opposite to the traditional restaurant which have their oven. Fattah has a burn teast. Food is seems prepared by non-natives to the countries of these traditional food so they don't know what is the real teast is! Tables and seats are comfortable and the over all experience is bad. Extremely over priced. I have tried it twice to make a true and honest judgment and results came very disappointed. It doesn't deserve one star not even zero but negative star!

I am a customer for this restaurant for more than 10 years. My father eats here since early 80’s. Their customer service has dropped drastically. The person who was taking my order left while I was talking because a customer in thob entered the restaurant while there were other waiters around. Later when I was eating, one waiter came and took the oil from my table that I was using and gave it to another customer who was also in thob. When I said I need the oil for my food, he started arguing.

This restaurant was good in the past. Today, see the photos, you get burn mankesh bread with burn cheese or zaatar. You really smell smoke while eating. The mankesh base is very thick as if you are biting something but not manakesh. Other meals have also similar issues. The guys were very polite during ordering, that makes us feel a delicious meals are being prepared. I don't really know what's happening. Unbelievable!
Good staffs nice behavior also delicious food.
Unfortunately, this restaurant fell short in every way. The food was not enjoyable, and the lack of cleanliness, particularly in the bathroom, was a major turn-off 🤮.
Do not go to this restaurant the worst  Service in Qatar/ they disrespect the costumers and the prices is soo high

We went to this restaurant yesterday as we saw it in documentary movie by DW Channel , we were very excited to try their signature falafel and traditional Lebanese food but it was very disappointing visit,
We ordered foul, meat with hummus, flafel , water and pepsi .
The waiter came back after approximately 10 min with foul , meat with hummus green olive, red onion and water . Their was no bread to eat food with it , we asked him to bring bread and pepsi and we waited for another 7 minute’s then he came with the bread only
Then we waited for another 10 min and remained him to bring pepsi 2 times but the response was very slow. After that my husband got mad and cancelled flafel and we left the restaurant . Food taste wasn’t special at all and we didn’t liked it.

With better service, this place could be perfect.

While the food was enjoyable, the overall experience was let down by the subpar atmosphere and poor service. The family section, in particular, was quite disappointing. With only two staff members present, it was evident they were overwhelmed and unable to manage the area effectively. Their behavior was unusual, possibly due to the pressure of frequent orders , and at times, they even displayed visible frustration towards customers.

When I brought this to the attention of the cashier on duty, his response was dismissive, simply stating that there was nothing he could do. At that point, I chose not to pursue the matter further, as it was clear that customer service was not a priority. A disappointing experience overall, despite the good food.

The hummus is bland and poor quality, the fava beans lack texture and taste bland too, the olive oil is low-grade. They don’t even serve fresh vegetables with the foul and hummus, unheard of for a Lebanese restaurant serving these staples. Falafel is saturated with oil, not crispy as you would expect. owners doesn't seem to care about the feedback and constructive criticism to improve. Honestly, this place is perhaps the worst representation of Lebanese cuisine in Qatar
Over hyped. Definitely not worth it

After a long day of hard work, I decided that a chicken shawarma would be a good dinner. Usually, a shawarma from Beirut would be one of my favourites. After today I do not think I will be ordering a shawarma from here any time soon.

The shawarma was made on supermarket pita bread and did not have the flavour of an Arabic shawarma. It was extremely dry with it having only a touch of garlic. The chicken too was not upto speed. The fries and pickles are pretty good but I'm not buying a fries-and-pickle sandwich. The 10 riyal price tag will never be justifiable for this abomination. Please do better.
